skill.name: Pick the best one-sentence summary
skill.why: A good summary proves you understood the whole text, not just one bit.
skill.how: Cover the whole text. Reject summaries that are too narrow, too broad or untrue.

steps.say: A summary squeezes a whole story into one sentence.
steps.ask: Which sentence tells the whole story?

options.text: Mo flipped a pancake.
options.reason: That's only the start. What happened next?

options.text: Mo's pancake stuck to the ceiling, so everyone ate cereal.
Mo made perfect pancakes for everyone.
options.reason: Perfect? It stuck to the ceiling! Check every part against the story.

steps.win: Yes! It covers the start, middle and end.

steps.say: Each weak summary has its own problem.

show.nudge: That's true, but is it one small bit? It hardly says anything.
Was it perfect? That one gets a fact wrong.

show.text: Mo's pancake stuck to the ceiling, so everyone ate cereal.
show.nudge: That's the best summary. Find one that grabs only one bit.

steps.ask: Tap the one that's true, but only tells one small bit.
steps.win: Yes! True, but only the start. That's too narrow.

show.nudge: That's the too-narrow one. It tells one small bit.
That one isn't even true. Find one that's true but tells you nothing.

show.text: Mo's pancake stuck to the ceiling, so everyone ate cereal.
show.nudge: That's the best summary. It says exactly what happened.

steps.ask: Tap the one that's true, but doesn't say what happened.
steps.win: Yes! Too broad means so general it skips the story.

steps.say: Careful! Too broad can sound clever.

show.text: Rosie the school goat ate the footy.
With no ball, the game stopped.
So everyone played chasey with Rosie instead.

options.text: A school footy game did not go the way anyone planned.
options.reason: True, but what happened? It never says goat, footy or chasey. Too broad.

options.text: Rosie ate the footy, so everyone played chasey with her instead.
Rosie the school goat ate the footy.
options.reason: True, but it stops at the start. What did everyone do next? Too narrow.

steps.win: Yes! 'Not the way anyone planned' sounds good, but says nothing.

steps.say: Last check. Test each part against the story.

show.nudge: Rosie is the goat. That part's true.
She did eat the footy. That part's true.

steps.ask: Tap the part of this summary that's untrue.
steps.win: Yes! They played chasey. One wrong fact makes it untrue.

terms.means: Covers the whole text, start to end, and every part is true.
True, but only one small bit. It skips the rest.
True, but so general it doesn't say what actually happened.
Gets a fact wrong. Check every part against the text.

examples.text: Mo's pancake stuck to the ceiling, so everyone ate cereal.
A school footy game did not go the way anyone planned.
Rosie ate the footy, so everyone went home.

card.test: Does it cover the whole text? Is every part true? Does it say what happened?

weDo.text: Gus left a banana in his schoolbag over the holidays. When he opened the bag, it was black and squishy. Tiny flies buzzed out. His homework was glued together with banana goo.
weDo.hint: Which one covers the whole story and gets every fact right?
weDo.success: It covers the whole story: the forgotten banana and the gross mess it made.

options.text: A banana Gus forgot in his bag rotted and made a gross mess.
Tiny flies buzzed out of Gus's bag.
options.reason: Too narrow. The flies are one small detail, not the whole story.

options.text: Gus ate a banana from his schoolbag.
options.reason: Untrue. Read the first sentence again. What did Gus do with the banana?

weDo.text: Wren found a joey in a ditch after a storm. It was cold and wet. She wrapped it in her jumper and carried it to the vet hut. A week later, it was hopping around and eating grass.
weDo.hint: Watch out for a summary that names who, but never says what happened.
weDo.success: It says who, what happened and how it ended, all in one true sentence.

options.text: Something happened to Wren and a joey after a big storm.
options.reason: Too broad. It names Wren and the joey, but what actually happened to them?

options.text: Wren rescued a cold joey after a storm and nursed it back to health.
Wren wrapped a joey in her jumper.
options.reason: Too narrow. It skips how she found the joey and how it got better.

creature.name: Gulpelli
creature.blurb: A pelican that swallows a whole story in one gulp. It spits out any summary that's too small, too big or untrue.

write.ask: Write one sentence that sums up this whole story.
given: Mo's sandwich fell into a rock pool.
Gus reached in to grab it, but a crab grabbed his finger.
Then Wren lifted the crab off and saved the sandwich too.
checks: It covers the start and the end.
Every part of it is true.
write.model: When Gus reached into a rock pool for Mo's sandwich and a crab grabbed his finger, Wren saved them both.

encounters.frame: Mo's diary has washed up next to a hungry Gulpelli.
encounters.text: Mo decided to bake a birthday cake for Tully. He did not have any sugar. So he used salt instead. He thought nobody would notice. The cake looked amazing. It had pink icing and ten candles. Tully took a huge bite. Her face went bright red. She ran to the tap and drank for a full minute. Mo tasted the cake too. Then he ran to the tap as well.
encounters.prompt: Which is the best summary?
encounters.success: It covers the whole story: the salt swap and what happened when they tasted it.

options.text: Mo used salt instead of sugar, so Tully's cake tasted awful.
Tully's birthday cake looked amazing, with pink icing and ten candles.
options.reason: Too narrow. It's true, but it only tells you how the cake looked.

options.text: Mo baked Tully a delicious birthday cake.
options.reason: Untrue. They both ran to the tap, so the cake was not delicious.

encounters.frame: Wren has pinned a sign to the vet hut. The Gulpelli wants it in one gulp.
encounters.text: LOST: one baby wombat. Her name is Pudding. She is small, round and brown. She escaped this morning through a hole in the fence. She loves carrots and muddy holes. She is not dangerous. She might nibble your shoelaces, though. If you see Pudding, please do not chase her. Call Wren at the vet hut instead. We miss her very much!
encounters.prompt: Which is the best summary of the sign?
encounters.success: It says what the sign is about and what Wren wants you to do.

options.text: Pudding is small, round and brown, and she loves carrots and muddy holes.
options.reason: Too narrow. It's true, but it skips that she is lost.

options.text: Wren's sign tells you about a baby wombat called Pudding.
options.reason: Too broad. It names Pudding, but what's wrong, and what should you do?

options.text: Pudding the wombat is lost, so call Wren if you see her.

encounters.frame: Tully is reading out the space news. The Gulpelli is listening.
encounters.text: Astronauts on a space station had a messy problem last week. A bag of honey burst open. There is almost no gravity on the station, so the honey did not fall. It floated around in big golden blobs. One blob stuck to a computer screen. Another landed in the captain's hair. The crew spent six hours catching blobs with straws. Now all honey must be kept in a locked box.
encounters.prompt: Which is the best summary?
encounters.success: It covers the burst, the floating blobs and the new rule, and it's all true.

options.text: Honey floated around a space station, so now it gets locked away.
A blob of honey landed in the captain's hair.
options.reason: Too narrow. That's one funny detail, not the whole report.

options.text: Astronauts dropped a bag of honey, and it fell and splashed across the floor.
options.reason: Untrue. Remember, there is almost no gravity on the station.

encounters.frame: Tully's footy report has five summaries. The Gulpelli will only swallow one.
encounters.text: The Reef Rays were losing by five points. There was one minute left. Then it started to hail. Most players ran for cover. But Kira, the smallest Ray, kept going. She grabbed the ball out of a puddle. She kicked it from the boundary line. It wobbled through the air and went straight through the posts. The Rays won by one point!
encounters.prompt: Match each summary to the right label.
encounters.success: The best summary covers the whole report and gets every fact right.

items.text: Kira kicked a goal in the hail to win the game for the Rays.
items.reason: Does it cover the start, the middle and the end of the report?

items.text: Kira, the tallest Ray, kicked a goal to win the game.
items.reason: Check how the report describes Kira. Was she the tallest Ray?

items.text: Kira grabbed the ball out of a puddle.
items.reason: Is this the whole report, or one moment? Does it say who won?

items.text: This report is about a sport.
items.reason: Could this fit any sports report? Does it say what happened?

items.text: The Reef Rays lost the game in the hail.
items.reason: Check the last line of the report. How many points did the Rays win by?

encounters.frame: Zed read his diary to the crew. Indi wrote a summary, but one part is wrong.
encounters.text: Last night I heard scratching in the roof. Scratch, scratch, scratch. I hid under my blanket. I was sure it was a ghost. In the morning, Dad climbed up with a torch. He found a mother possum and three babies. They had made a nest out of Dad's old socks. Now we leave them apples every night. The scratching still wakes me up, but I don't mind.
encounters.prompt: Tap the part of the summary that is wrong, then choose a better one.
encounters.success: A mother possum and her babies. That's what Dad found, so now the summary is true.

parts.reason: That part is right. The diary starts with scratching in the roof.

parts: in Zed's roof turned out to be

parts.reason: That part is right. Zed says they leave apples every night.

options.text: a mother possum and her babies
a pile of Dad's old socks
options.reason: The socks were only the nest. Who made the nest?

options.text: a big hungry rat
options.reason: Untrue. Look again at what Dad found with his torch.

encounters.frame: Gus wrote about his newest invention. The Gulpelli is waiting for a summary.
encounters.text: Gus built a robot to tidy his room. He called it Neatbot. On the first day, Neatbot picked up every sock. On the second day, it folded all his shirts. On the third day, it tried to throw out his slime collection. Gus grabbed the jars just in time. He was furious. He took out Neatbot's batteries. Now his room is messy again, but his slime is safe.
encounters.prompt: Which is the best summary?
encounters.success: It covers the robot, the slime problem and how Gus stopped it.

options.text: Neatbot folded Gus's shirts on the second day.
options.reason: Too narrow. That's just day two. It skips the slime and the batteries.

options.text: Gus switched off his tidying robot after it tried to bin his slime.
Gus built a tidying robot that still keeps his whole room neat for him.
options.reason: Untrue. Gus took out its batteries, and his room is messy again.

encounters.frame: Zed posted a game review on the island noticeboard. The Gulpelli is circling it.
encounters.text: Zed's review: Turtle Tumble 3. I waited two years for Turtle Tumble 3, and the first level is brilliant. You roll a turtle down a waterfall while dodging hungry eels. The music is catchy and the colours are bright. Then everything goes wrong. On level four, the game froze six times. On level five, my turtle fell through the floor and never came back. I restarted twice, and exactly the same thing happened. The boss battle looked amazing in the ads, but I never even reached it. If the makers fix the bugs, this could be a great game. Right now, save your pocket money.
encounters.prompt: Which is the best summary of the review?
encounters.success: It covers the good start, the bugs and Zed's advice, which is the whole review.

options.text: Turtle Tumble 3 starts brilliantly, but bugs ruin it, so wait for a fix.
Zed loved the bright colours and catchy music in Turtle Tumble 3.
options.reason: Too narrow. That's only the first level. Most of the review is about the bugs.

options.text: Zed finally beat the boss battle but thought the game was far too short and easy.
options.reason: Untrue. Zed says he never even reached the boss battle.

encounters.frame: A soggy newspaper is floating past the Gulpelli's beak.
encounters.text: Staff at the Hollowgum Aquarium were puzzled. Every morning, another crab was missing from Tank 6. The lid on the tank was never broken. So keepers set up cameras to catch the thief. The footage showed Biscuit, the aquarium's octopus. Each night, she squeezed through a gap in her own lid no wider than a coin. She slid across the floor, climbed into Tank 6 and ate a crab. Then she crawled back home before sunrise. Keepers have now fixed her lid with heavy clips. Biscuit does not seem pleased. She has started squirting water at anyone who walks past.
encounters.prompt: Which is the best summary of the news story?
encounters.success: It names the thief, what she did and how the keepers stopped her.

options.text: Biscuit squirts water at people who walk past her tank.
options.reason: Too narrow. That's how the story ends, but it skips the crab thefts.

options.text: Cameras showed the crabs were escaping each night through a gap in their own tank lid.
options.reason: Untrue. The crabs went missing, but look at who the cameras actually showed.

options.text: An octopus sneaked out at night to eat crabs until keepers clipped her lid.

encounters.frame: Gus has written a fact file. Help the Gulpelli sort the summaries.
encounters.text: Gus's fact file: owl pellets. Owls swallow mice, frogs and beetles whole. But they can't digest every part. The bones, fur and feathers stay behind in their stomach. Every day or so, the owl squeezes this leftover mess into a tight ball. Then it coughs the ball back up and spits it out. This ball is called a pellet. Scientists love pellets. By pulling one apart, they can find tiny skulls and work out exactly what the owl ate. Gus found a pellet under a gum tree last week. He says it smelled like a wet dog. He took it to school anyway.
encounters.prompt: Match each summary to the right label.
encounters.success: The best summary explains what a pellet is and why scientists care, and every part is true.

items.text: Owls cough up pellets of bones and fur, and scientists study them to see what owls eat.
items.reason: It covers what pellets are and why scientists love them, and it's all true.

items.text: Gus found a smelly pellet under a gum tree.
items.reason: It's true, but it's only the ending. It doesn't explain what a pellet is.

items.text: This fact file is about something birds do.
items.reason: It's true, but it could fit a fact file about nests, eggs or flying.

items.text: Owls cough up pellets, and scientists study them to work out how old owls are.
items.reason: Check what scientists work out from a pellet. Is it how old the owl is?

items.text: Owls chew up bones and fur so they can digest every part of a mouse.
items.reason: The fact file says owls can't digest bones and fur. They cough them up.

encounters.frame: Mo is posting a letter. The Gulpelli snatched it to read first.
encounters.text: Dear Music Club, thank you for lending me a drum kit. Sadly, there have been a few problems. On Monday, I practised in our shed for three hours. On Tuesday, our neighbour asked me to stop because her baby couldn't sleep. On Wednesday, a flock of cockatoos landed on the shed roof and screeched along with every beat. On Thursday, Mum said the shed was out of bounds. So I have moved my drums to the empty end of the beach. The only one who complains there is a seagull. I would like to borrow the kit for another month, please. From Mo
encounters.prompt: Which is the best summary of Mo's letter?
encounters.success: It covers the problems, the move to the beach and what Mo is asking for.

options.text: Mo is writing to say sorry for the noise and to give the drum kit back.
options.reason: Untrue. Read the end of the letter. What does Mo ask for?

options.text: After complaints at home, Mo took the drums to the beach and wants them longer.
A flock of cockatoos screeched along with Mo's drumming.
options.reason: Too narrow. That's one of the problems. It skips the beach and Mo's request.

encounters.frame: Indi wants her mural story summed up. The Gulpelli has scrambled the pieces.
encounters.text: Indi painted a huge whale on the school wall. It took her three weekends and forty tins of blue paint. On Monday morning, she found that someone had painted a curly moustache on her whale. Indi was upset at first. She had worked so hard, and now her whale looked like a grumpy old uncle. Then she noticed that everyone was laughing and taking photos. Kids from other schools came to see it. So Indi added a top hat and a monocle too. Nobody ever found out who painted the moustache. The principal now calls the mural Sir Whale and says it can stay forever. Indi has started painting a walrus on the other wall, just in case.
encounters.prompt: Tap the pieces in order to build the best summary.
encounters.success: It covers the prank, how everyone reacted and what Indi did next.

tiles: Someone painted a moustache on Indi's whale mural,
Indi used forty tins of paint,
so she made it even funnier.
accept: Someone painted a moustache on Indi's whale mural, but everyone loved it, so she made it even funnier.
body.reason: Start with the prank, then how people reacted, then what Indi did. Indi wasn't upset for long.

encounters.frame: Maxx Vantablack is streaming from Hollowgum Island. Indi summed it up, but one part misses the point.
encounters.text: Hey, Vanta-fans! It's your hero, Maxx Vantablack, live from Hollowgum Island. Today I am rescuing a super-rare Gulpelli. Look, there it is, sitting on that log. Look at the size of that beak! Chat, I'm basically a wildlife expert at this point. I'm creeping closer. My net is ready. Shh. Got it! Wait, it's wriggling. Ow! It bit my thumb! It's flapping away! It's landed in the swamp! OK, fans, that was totally the camera guy's fault. He sneezed. Anyway, I'm not even hurt. Well, my thumb is a bit purple. No, I'm not crying. My eyes are just sweaty. Smash that like button, because tomorrow I'm catching two of them.
encounters.prompt: Tap the part of the summary that misses the main event, then choose a better one.
encounters.success: The bite and the escape are what actually happened, so they belong in the summary.

parts.reason: That part is right. It's Maxx's stream, and he's the one trying.
That part is right. He says he's live.

options.text: it bit him and escaped into the swamp
he caught two of them the next day
options.reason: Untrue. Maxx only says he'll try tomorrow. The stream doesn't show it.

options.text: he had his net ready
options.reason: Too narrow. The net is a small detail. What happened once Maxx grabbed it?

encounters.frame: Zed wrote up the lighthouse mystery. The Gulpelli gulps only the best summary.
encounters.text: For three weeks, a strange light had been flickering at the top of the old Hollowgum lighthouse. Nobody had lived there for fifty years. Locals whispered that the ghost of the last keeper had come back to tend his lamp. Some said they had heard footsteps on the stairs and smelled something burning. Zed and Tully decided to find out the truth. At midnight, they crept up the spiral staircase with a torch and a camera. The burning smell grew stronger with every step. At the top, they flung open the door. There, sitting on an upturned bucket, was Mo. He was holding a frying pan over a tiny camping stove. Mo had been sneaking out to cook midnight snacks where nobody would complain about the smoke. The flickering was his head torch, which had a loose battery. Mo offered them each a burnt pancake. Zed said it was the scariest thing he'd seen all night.
encounters.prompt: Which is the best summary?
encounters.success: It covers the mystery and the answer: who was up there and why. Every part is true.

options.text: Zed and Tully climbed the lighthouse at midnight to find out if a ghost was making the light.
options.reason: It's true, but it stops halfway. What did they find at the top?

options.text: After weeks of ghost stories, a lighthouse mystery that had the town whispering finally had a surprising answer.
options.reason: Too broad. It sounds clever, but what was the answer? It never says.

options.text: A spooky light in the old lighthouse turned out to be Mo cooking secret midnight snacks.
The flickering light at the top of the lighthouse was a head torch with a loose battery.
options.reason: Too narrow. It explains the flicker, but whose torch, and what were they doing up there?

encounters.frame: Tully's carnival report has five summaries. Help the Gulpelli sort them.
encounters.text: The Hollowgum School relay team had trained all year for the district swimming carnival. Then, on the morning of the race, their fastest swimmer, Priya, woke up with a fever. The team needed a fourth swimmer, and the only one left was Sam. Sam had only learnt to swim properly the year before. He had never raced in front of a crowd. He was so nervous that he put his cap on inside out. The first three swimmers kept the team in fourth place. Then Sam dived in for the last leg. He didn't swim with perfect style, but he never stopped kicking. Slowly, he passed one swimmer, then another. The crowd was on its feet, and even the other schools were cheering for him. The team touched the wall in second place, their best result ever. Their coach said she had never seen anyone kick so hard. Priya watched the race on a video call from her bed and cheered so loudly that her mum came running in.
encounters.prompt: Match each summary to the right label.
encounters.success: The best summary covers the problem, Sam's swim and the result. Two near misses get a fact wrong.

items.text: With their fastest swimmer sick, the relay team relied on nervous Sam, who kicked them up to second.
items.reason: Does it cover the problem, who stepped in and how the race ended?

items.text: With Priya sick, Sam swam the first leg and kept the relay team in fourth place.
items.reason: Check which leg Sam swam. Who kept the team in fourth place?

items.text: Priya cheered from her bed so loudly that her mum came running in.
items.reason: Is this the whole report, or one moment near the end?

items.text: A school relay team had a carnival day that none of them will ever forget.
items.reason: What happened on that day? Does it name the problem or the result?

items.text: Sam swam the last leg after Priya got sick, and the team won the carnival.
items.reason: Check the end of the report. Where did the team touch the wall?

encounters.frame: The Hollowgum Museum has a new display card. The Gulpelli has jumbled up its summary.
encounters.text: When farmer Lyn Doyle found a heavy black rock in her sheep paddock, she thought it was a lump of old iron. She used it as a doorstop for eleven years. She nearly threw it in the dam more than once. Then a visiting geology student noticed the strange dimples on its surface and asked if she could test it. The results were astonishing. The rock was a meteorite, around four and a half billion years old. It had been drifting through space long before there were any dinosaurs, or even any oceans. Scientists believe it fell during a wild storm that Lyn remembers from the year she bought the farm. She had heard a bang like thunder, but she never saw anything land. The meteorite is now on display at the Hollowgum Museum. Some of the museum's experts cried when they first held it. Lyn visits it every month. She says she misses it, but mostly because her back door now slams shut every time the wind blows.
encounters.prompt: Tap the pieces in order to build the best summary. Check every piece is true.
encounters.success: Every piece is true. Lyn never saw it land, and her door slams because the rock is gone.

tiles: A doorstop Lyn kept for eleven years
A rock Lyn saw fall in a storm
turned out to be an ancient meteorite
turned out to be a lump of old iron
and is now in a museum.
and still holds her back door open.
accept: A doorstop Lyn kept for eleven years turned out to be an ancient meteorite and is now in a museum.
body.reason: Test each piece. Did Lyn see anything land? And why does her back door slam now?

encounters.frame: Wren's field diary is open on the Gulpelli's nest.
encounters.text: Every spring, the magpie by the school gate goes wild. This year it swooped Zed four times in one morning and once pulled a hair right out of his head. Zed started wearing a bike helmet all day, even inside. The principal wanted to call a ranger to move it. Wren asked for one week to try something else first. She found out that only male magpies swoop, and only while there are chicks in the nest. They aren't being cruel. They're guarding their babies. So Wren mapped a new route to school that went around the nest tree instead of under it. It took a little longer, but nobody minded. Indi painted big eyes on the back of everyone's hats, because magpies are less likely to swoop when they think they're being watched. By Friday, nobody had been swooped. The principal agreed to leave the magpie alone. In a few weeks, the chicks will fly, and the swooping will stop anyway.
encounters.prompt: Which is the best summary of Wren's diary?
encounters.success: It covers the problem, what Wren worked out and how it ended, without moving the bird.

options.text: After the magpie swooped Zed, Wren found out why and asked for a week to try another way.
options.reason: True, but it stops halfway. Did her plan work, and what did the principal decide?

options.text: Wren worked out why the magpie swooped and stopped the swooping without moving the bird.
Indi's painted eyes stopped the magpie swooping, so the principal let it stay.
options.reason: It gives the hats all the credit. What else was in Wren's plan?

options.text: The school gate magpie taught the school something about living with wildlife.
options.reason: Too broad. It sounds wise, but what happened? It never says.

encounters.frame: Tully summed up the festival notice, but one part leaves out the reason, so the Gulpelli won't swallow it.
encounters.text: Notice from the Hollowgum Festival Committee. For forty years, the highlight of our festival has been the Great Pumpkin Roll. Growers roll their giant pumpkins down Gumtree Hill, and the first to reach the bottom wins. Sadly, last year's winning pumpkin did not stop at the bottom. It bounced over the fence, rolled across the car park and smashed through the front window of the bakery. Nobody was hurt, but the bakery was closed for a month and the owner is still finding seeds. The committee has decided that the roll is now too dangerous. We know many of you will be disappointed, and so are we. This year, it will be replaced by the Great Pumpkin Paddle. Growers will hollow out their pumpkins and paddle them across Hollowgum Lake. Pumpkins must be grown by the person paddling them. Life jackets are compulsory. Prizes will be given for the fastest pumpkin and the best-decorated one. The baker has kindly agreed to judge the decorations.
encounters.prompt: Tap the part of the summary that leaves out the reason, then choose a better one.
encounters.success: The crash is why the committee calls the roll too dangerous. Now the summary gives the reason.

parts.reason: That part is right. The notice is about the end of the Pumpkin Roll.

parts.tap: replaced by a pumpkin boat race
parts.reason: That part is right. The Pumpkin Paddle is a race across the lake in pumpkins.

options.text: Because the baker wanted to judge a new contest
options.reason: The baker agreed to judge after the change. Why did the committee stop the roll?

options.text: Because last year's winning pumpkin smashed into the bakery
Because the pumpkins had grown too heavy to roll
options.reason: The notice never says that. What happened at the bottom of the hill last year?

encounters.frame: Gus found a notice from a robot company stuck to the Gulpelli's beak.
encounters.text: Important notice from Hollowgum Robotics. Last Tuesday, we sent an update to every Mowzo robot mower on the island. The update was supposed to make the mowers quieter. Instead, a mistake in the code made them mow only in circles. Owners woke up to lawns covered in rings, swirls and spirals. One Mowzo escaped its yard and mowed a giant smiley face into the middle of the footy oval, an hour before the grand final. We are very sorry, and we know some of you have spent years getting your lawns perfect. Please switch off your Mowzo and leave it on its charging pad. Do not try to fix your mower yourself, as this may make the problem worse. Tonight we will send a new update that fixes the problem, and your mower will restart by itself tomorrow morning. Owners who want their lawns repaired can call us for free help. The footy club has asked to keep the smiley face.
encounters.prompt: Which is the best summary of the notice?
encounters.success: It covers what went wrong and what owners should do, which is the point of the notice.

options.text: After a faulty update, one Mowzo escaped and mowed a giant smiley face into the footy oval.
options.reason: Too narrow. That is one mower. What went wrong for owners, and what should they do?

options.text: A faulty update made the mowers cut circles, so owners need to fix their own mowers tonight.
options.reason: Check what the notice says about fixing your mower yourself.

options.text: Hollowgum Robotics is sorry that its latest mower update did not go to plan.
options.reason: Too broad. What went wrong, and what should owners do? It never says.

options.text: A faulty update made mowers cut circles, so owners should switch them off until it's fixed.

encounters.frame: The Hollowgum Herald has landed in the Gulpelli's pouch. Zed and Tully each wrote a summary.
encounters.text: Every summer, volunteers wade into the rock pools at Hollowgum Point for the annual Sea Slug Count. Armed with buckets, magnifying glasses and waterproof notebooks, they spend a low tide searching under ledges and among the seaweed for nudibranchs, the brilliantly coloured sea slugs that live along the coast. Most years, the count is pleasant but unremarkable: volunteers record around thirty species, eat a sausage from the barbecue and go home. This year was different. Eleven-year-old Ruby Tan, attending for the first time, spotted a slug no longer than a grain of rice. It was electric purple with orange tips, and none of the experts recognised it. One of them was so surprised that she dropped her notebook in the pool. Photographs were sent to the state museum, where a marine biologist confirmed that the slug had never been described by science. Under the rules for naming animals, the scientist who formally describes a new species chooses its name, but she has invited Ruby to suggest one. Ruby is considering Grape Fizz. She admits she only came along because her grandmother made her, and she had planned to spend the day looking for crabs. Next year's count is expected to attract three times as many volunteers, and organisers have asked newcomers to tread carefully, because rock pools are fragile and the next undiscovered species could be underfoot.

encounters.frame: Zed recorded Maxx Vantablack's latest stream. Help the Gulpelli sort the crew's summaries.
encounters.text: Welcome back, Vanta-fans! Today is the day you've all been waiting for: the launch of my very own game, Vanta Rescue. In this game, you play as me, obviously, travelling the islands and saving rare creatures from danger. Watch this. I'm sneaking up on a wild Gulpelli, and, boom, it's in my rescue pod! Now it's safe forever. Listen to it squawking with happiness. Some of you in the chat are asking why the rescue pods have bars and padlocks. Great question. That's for the creatures' protection, because the outside world is extremely dangerous. Others are asking why there's no button to release them. Honestly, why would you want to? They're much happier with me, and if they're not happy, they'll learn to be. Right, let's check the leaderboard, because whoever rescues the most creatures by Sunday wins a signed hoodie. Hang on, someone's spamming the chat. They say the maps in my game match the real Hollowgum Island exactly, with every creature's nest marked. That's a total coincidence, and I'm deleting that comment. Moderators, please ban anyone who mentions maps. And no, my real rescue centre is not open to visitors, so stop asking. Let's move on to the next level, shall we? Tomorrow I'll be streaming from a secret location, so stay tuned.

encounters.frame: Gus wants a one-line summary of this story for his stink collection. He wrote two drafts.
encounters.text: Visitors to the Hollowgum Botanic Gardens are being warned to bring a peg for their noses. The gardens' corpse flower, a giant plant from the rainforests of Sumatra, has bloomed for the first time in seven years. Its single flower spike is taller than a grown adult, and its frilly purple skirt opened late on Tuesday night. The plant is named for its smell. To attract the flies and beetles that pollinate it, the flower gives off a stench that visitors have compared to rotting fish, sweaty socks and a bin left in the sun for a fortnight. It even warms itself up so that the smell spreads further. Since the news broke, the queue has stretched around the lake, with some people waiting three hours for a sniff. Even the ducks on the lake are keeping their distance, and school groups have been asked to write words for a smell warning at the gate. Head gardener Phil Okafor says the crowds should hurry, because the bloom lasts only about two days before the skirt closes and the spike collapses. Gardeners worked through the night to collect pollen, which will be shared with other gardens so that more corpse flowers can be grown. 'It's disgusting,' said one visitor, holding her nose. 'I'm coming back tomorrow.'

encounters.success: Draft 1 stops at the bloom. Draft 2 adds the queues and the rush, the heart of the story.

encounters.frame: Tully is reading the ferry news aloud while the Gulpelli waits for its catch.
encounters.text: For thirty-one years, Arthur Penhaligon has stood beside the ticket gates at the Hollowgum ferry terminal, playing the same tune on a carpenter's saw. He bends the blade with one hand and draws a violin bow across it with the other, producing an eerie, wobbling sound that commuters describe as a ghost singing in the shower. Nobody knows the name of the song, and Arthur refuses to tell. Regulars swear they could set their watches by his first note, which sounds at exactly seven o'clock every morning. Last month, the council introduced new rules banning all performers from the terminal, saying the walkway had become too crowded at peak hour. Arthur was moved to a quiet corner of the car park, where hardly anyone passed. Within a week, commuters had noticed the silence, and ferry staff said the mornings felt strangely empty. A schoolgirl started a petition, which was signed by more than four thousand people, and passengers began humming Arthur's tune as they walked through the gates in protest. On Monday, the council announced that one performer would be allowed back at the terminal, as long as they stood clear of the walkway. The spot was offered to Arthur. He celebrated by playing his song twice, which regulars say has never happened before. He still won't reveal its name.

encounters.success: It covers the move, the commuters' campaign and Arthur's return, which is the whole story in order.

encounters.frame: Indi summed up an art scandal for the Gulpelli. One part of the summary is wrong.
encounters.text: When the judges of the Hollowgum Art Prize announced this year's winner, the crowd at the gallery burst into applause. The winning work, titled Storm Over the Bay, was a huge canvas covered in swirls of blue, splashes of yellow and a mysterious brown smudge in one corner. One judge called it fearless, and another said it captured the chaos of nature. The artist, a quiet sculptor named Dev Marsh, accepted the prize of two thousand dollars and said very little. Several art students wrote essays about the work's hidden meaning. A week later, he admitted the truth in a letter to the local paper. Storm Over the Bay was not a painting at all. It was the old cloth he spreads across his studio floor to catch drips while he works on other pieces. He had entered it as a joke, never expecting to be shortlisted, and the brown smudge was a coffee stain. Some locals demanded that the prize be taken back. However, the judges met again and decided that Dev could keep it, because, as their statement put it, art is about how a work makes you feel. Dev has since donated the prize money to the school art room, and the cloth now hangs in the gallery's front window.

encounters.frame: Mo cut this story out of the paper and stuck it on the galley fridge. The Gulpelli wants a summary.
encounters.text: The Hollowgum Bakery had spent months planning its attempt to bake the world's largest lamington. The sponge alone weighed as much as a small car, and it took twelve bakers, three wheelbarrows of coconut and a forklift to assemble. The official measurement was booked for midday on Saturday in the town square. Unfortunately, Saturday turned out to be the hottest day of the year. By eleven o'clock, the chocolate icing had begun to slide off the sides, and by half past, the whole cake had slumped into a gooey brown puddle that was attracting every fly on the island. Some children were spotted eating the fallen coconut straight off the cobblestones. The record judge, who had travelled from the mainland, shook her head and explained that a lamington must hold its shape. Rather than give up, head baker Rosa Liu grabbed a microphone and asked the crowd for help. Within an hour, locals had carried over buckets of custard, jelly and cream from their kitchens, and the bakers layered it all, melted lamington included, into an empty paddling pool. The judge measured the result and confirmed it as the world's largest trifle, a record nobody had ever attempted before. The bakery says it will try the lamington again, this time in winter. The forklift driver says he will never look at a lamington the same way again.

encounters.success: It covers the melted lamington, the town's help and the new record, without getting any facts wrong.
